Noise cancelation (ANC) has three modes, on, transparency, and off. The noise cancelation (on) is very good (very quiet), transparency electronically pipes in outside (ambient) sounds, off is just that, but these headphones are so well sealed, that they provide passive noise reduction even when off (just by the well-fitting earcup insulation). So, the transparency setting is useful if I need/want to be aware of what's going on around me. A voice tells me which ANC mode is activated (or off). I also haven't tried them for phone quality (not why I bought them), I'll update this review once I try that feature out. Comparing the sound to an OLD (2016) pair of Bose QC35 headphones (Bluetooth 4.1), the QC35's have a distinctly better, more balanced sound, but they also cost nearly $350 when they came out some 10 years ago.
